BrandKitOut.description:
`status`: `filled` (every filled field confirmed), `guessed` (some filled field is a
first guess, e.g. drafted by `brandkit init --from`), `broken` (the kit does not load).
BrandKitOut.title: BrandKitOut

Brief.description:
What the viewer sees, in words -- human-typed or agent-drafted (`brief.write` in
fake mode). Distinct from `Span.note`, which is a regenerate instruction, not the brief
itself.
Brief.title: Brief

BudgetSetRequest.description:
T31: the only way a budget comes to exist. `unit` is the provider's own (`credits`
for Higgsfield, `usd` for Deepgram) -- required, never defaulted.
BudgetSetRequest.title: BudgetSetRequest

Cut.description: One edit of a project: a specific arrangement of passages and spans.
Cut.title: Cut

Passage.description: A run of words from one SyncGroup, played back through one angle (Source).
Passage.title: Passage

Rational.description: An exact rational number (e.g. frame rate 30000/1001), never a lossy float.
Rational.title: Rational

RunRequest.description:
T31: no `cap`/`unit` -- a budget is created only by `PUT .../budgets/{id}`, never as a
side effect of running. `budget` must already exist (else 409); `node_ids` limits the
authorisation to exactly the spending nodes the person was shown.
RunRequest.title: RunRequest

Section.description: A named grouping of passages within a Cut (e.g. a beat or chapter).
Section.title: Section

Shoot.description:
A recording session grouping sources, sync groups and transcripts.

Source and SyncGroup are small and embedded directly (there is no `sources/` or
`sync_groups/` directory in the store layout). Transcript is large (word lists) and
lives in its own file under `transcripts/`, referenced here by id only.
Shoot.title: Shoot

Source.description:
One recorded media file (video or audio) belonging to a shoot -- or (T23) a
`kind="virtual"` source with no underlying media at all, standing in for a locked cut
that Post never plays back (script-as-transcript demos).
Source.title: Source

Span.description:
A word-anchored region on one layer: picture (B-roll), overlay, or audio.

A beat pairs a `layer="picture"` span with an optional `layer="overlay"` span sharing
the same anchors (see module docstring). `overlay_depth`/`overlay_position` are set only
on overlay spans; `flags`/`cast_refs`/`density_hint`/`continuity_of_span_id` describe the
beat and are conventionally carried on its picture span.
Span.title: Span

SpeakersOut.description:
T35: each speaker label, its name (None until someone names it) and its longest
utterance as a sample. `source_id` is the recording whose audio proxy plays the samples
(`GET .../media/{source_id}/audio`).
SpeakersOut.title: SpeakersOut

SuggestionPatch.description:
T40: inline edits on a proposed card. Only the fields sent are changed; `medium: null`
means "overlay only" (refused unless the proposal carries an overlay).
SuggestionPatch.title: SuggestionPatch

SuggestionVariantOut.description: T42: one idea for a proposal's words ("Variant A", "Variant B", ...).
SuggestionVariantOut.title: SuggestionVariantOut

SyncGroup.description: A set of Sources locked to a shared timeline (e.g. multicam + external audio).
SyncGroup.title: SyncGroup

TranscriptMetaOut.description:
A Transcript's metadata without its (possibly huge) `words` list -- see `/words` for
those, paged.
TranscriptMetaOut.title: TranscriptMetaOut

Trim.description: Extra trim applied at the head/tail of a Passage's word range, in seconds.
Trim.title: Trim

VisualSuggestionOut.description:
T13b/T30b: one pending automated "Suggest visuals" proposal -- distinct from
`SuggestionOut` (the older filler/silence removal suggestions). T30b: carries the full
beat model (`medium` + optional overlay depth/position/flags), not just a layer bucket.
VisualSuggestionOut.title: VisualSuggestionOut

WordAnchor.description: Points at one word in one transcript. The unit of truth for edit-time anchoring.
WordAnchor.title: WordAnchor

No project needed: what the shell reads once to decide on its REAL badge.

Register (or re-register) a project by root path, initialising its `.post3/` store
if needed, and open it (starts its background queue-draining thread).

get.description:
The project's cast registry (T12), with each entry's continuity-anchor readiness --
feeds the graph's `character` node picker (T30d).

post.description:
No cast-authoring UI exists yet (T12's own scope) -- this exists so the graph's
`character` node picker (T30d) and its e2e have a real entry to reference; a full cast
registry UI is future work.

get.description:
T30e: the `aroll.regenerate` recipe's `consent.gate` reads `has_consent`/`read_consent`
directly (`recipes.instantiate_extra.maybe_preapprove_consent`) -- this is the human-facing
read: no record yet is not an error, just `recorded: false` with the other fields unset.
Every Cut in the project (master + derived), for the cut switcher.

post.description:
Instantiate the recipe for one span's kind and record the new workflow's id on the
span. Idempotent: a span that already has a `workflow_id` just returns it (re-adding a
visual to an already-planned beat should not silently orphan the existing graph).

T30b card action ("+3 more"): grow an already-instantiated `live_action` span's
workflow with `body.count` more `still.generate` nodes sharing its existing pick node
(`recipes.instantiate.add_more_stills`).

Run the pass (whole cut, or the given selection) and return every currently-pending
proposal. T42: the run replaces the pending proposals inside its scope (those elsewhere
stay); the project's picture mode steers it (`audio_only` = full coverage).
T42: make another of the proposal's ideas (Variant A, B, ...) the active one.

Other word ranges (any sync group) whose text fuzzy-matches the selection, for the
'Swap take' toolbar action. `cut_id` is accepted for routing symmetry but the search runs
over every transcript in the project, not just this cut's passages.

Ordered playback segments for the monitor: which source plays, and where, per passage.
The client never recomputes timeline maths -- it only follows this list.

post.description: Run the project's last ingest again: finished steps skip, failed/missing ones run.

Queue it. No budget -> 402; an unknown budget -> 409; an estimate past the budget's
headroom -> 402 (the app's spend handlers); no audio proxy -> 400; already has a
transcript -> 409.

Import a finished transcript file (JSON/SRT/VTT) for one recording. Free -- never a
provider call. Refuses a recording that already has one.

get.description:
Every node type the app can build a node from, the handle-type vocabulary
`isValidConnection` checks edges against, and the model choices for the node types that
expose a `model` param. T39: every image/video model `higgsfield model list` offers
(cached in `.post3/`, refreshed by `POST .../models/refresh`), labelled with its display
name; only the ones in `MODEL_OPTIONS` carry a price and capability chips.

The project's `provided/` folder catalogue (T30 taxonomy: footage the editor
supplies, not generated) -- fixture-backed for the demo per the task spec.

Every Shoot in the project, each carrying its Sources (angles), SyncGroups, and
`transcript_ids` -- the only place a client can resolve a Cut passage's `sync_group_id`
to the Transcript that holds its words, or an `angle_source_id` to a playable Source.

'Remove fillers' / 'Remove long silences' candidate ranges. Never auto-applied --
the client turns an accepted one into a normal `delete_words` op.

post.description:
Add and/or remove edges in one call, type-checked (`graph.workflow.assert_valid`)
against the node registry's handle types before anything is persisted.

patch.description:
T27 item 5 follow-up to T26: persist the graph view's drag positions into `Workflow.
layout` (UI-only, never read by hashing.py/state.py) so re-opening the graph doesn't
always re-run dagre auto-layout from scratch. Layout writes are last-write-wins and don't
need the caller's revision -- retries once on a save race against another writer.

schema.title: Response Workflow Update Layout Api Projects  Pid  Workflows  Workflow Id  Layout Patch

get.description:
State + input_hash + (if built) manifest outputs for every node -- one call the card
and graph views poll instead of re-deriving hashes/artifact paths client-side. `outputs`
entries carry whatever `sha256` the worker declared, which the client resolves through
`GET /api/projects/{pid}/assets/{sha256}` (`routes/media.py`) to render a thumbnail or
clip.

schema.title: Response Workflow Nodes Api Projects  Pid  Workflows  Workflow Id  Nodes Get

post.description:
Append one new, unwired node (e.g. the graph view's "+ reference image" palette
button, which adds a `source.file` node the user then connects to a `still.generate`
node's `continuity` input via `POST .../edges`) -- id auto-generated if omitted,
params validated against the type's own schema, whole graph re-validated before save.

delete.description:
T29 graph palette: delete a node and every edge touching it. A `pick` node whose
`selected` edge was just removed loses that selection too, so it never dangles on an
edge id that no longer exists (the same invariant `graph.workflow.validate` enforces).

patch.description:
Merge new param values into one node, re-validate its params against its NodeType's
schema and the whole workflow's wiring, and save. Stale propagation needs no extra work
here: it is derived (`graph.state.compute_states`), never stored -- changing a node's
params changes its `input_hash` the next time anything reads state/plan, which is what
marks it (and everything downstream) stale.

get.description:
A node's current artifact (if it has ever run and passed its check), as
`{sha256, url, ...extra-manifest-fields}` per output -- `url` points at the existing
content-addressed `/assets/{sha256}` route, so a card/graph-view thumbnail or clip
player never needs to know an artifact directory's on-disk layout.

schema.title: Response Node Artifact Api Projects  Pid  Workflows  Workflow Id  Nodes  Node Id  Artifact Get

post.description:
Refusals come from `enqueue()` (the core enforces them, not this route) and map to
JSON in `errors.py`: no authorisation / estimate past headroom / unit mismatch -> 402,
a budget that was never created -> 409. A refused run persists nothing.
